blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: build simple sentences in the right order
make negative sentences, including with nunca, nada and nadie
ask yes/no questions and questions with a question word
link ideas with y, o, pero and porque, and use the first prepositions correctly

blocks.text: The basic order is (subject) + verb + the rest. The subject is usually left out. Time and place expressions can go at the end or at the start, but the verb does not move.

items: Adjectives go after the noun: una casa grande, un coche rojo (PDF 5).
Time words can open the sentence: Hoy trabajo en casa. or Trabajo en casa hoy.

blocks.title: No Dutch word-order tricks needed
bullets: Dutch inverts after a time word (Morgen werk ik). Spanish does not: Mañana trabajo.
Dutch sends the verb to the end after omdat, dat, als. Spanish keeps the normal order: porque estoy cansado (omdat ik moe ben).

blocks.text: Put no directly before the verb: No hablo francés. No vivo en Madrid. The negative words below follow one rule: if they come after the verb, you also need no before the verb. If they come before the verb, you do not.

blocks.title: Double negatives are normal
blocks.text: Dutch and English avoid two negatives (ik zie niemand). Spanish requires them after the verb: No veo a nadie, No tengo nada.

items: Spanish has no helper like do or does. The same verb form does the job.
In Spain, if you state the subject in a question it goes after the verb: ¿Dónde vives (tú)?
To answer, repeat the verb: ¿Hablas inglés? Sí, hablo inglés. / No, no hablo inglés. (A negative answer starts with No, and then a negative sentence.)

Meaning
Example
rows: Es caro, pero es muy bueno.

blocks.title: y becomes e, o becomes u
blocks.text:
y changes to e before a word that starts with i- or hi-: español e inglés, padre e hijo (but agua y hielo, because of hie-).
o changes to u before a word that starts with o- or ho-: siete u ocho, mujer u hombre.

head: Word
Main uses
Example
rows: Voy a Madrid. Llego a las dos. Veo a María.
Soy de España. Es el libro de Ana.
Estoy en casa. Voy en tren.
Es para ti. Estudio para aprender.
Trabajo desde las nueve hasta las cinco.
Está entre el banco y la farmacia.

items: Personal a: put a before a direct object that is a specific person (or a pet): Veo a Pedro. Conozco a tu hermana. Not before things: Veo la tele. Not after tener: Tengo dos hermanos.
Possession uses de, never 's: el libro de Ana (Ana's book).

blocks.text: El gato está debajo de la mesa. La farmacia está al lado del banco. Mi casa está lejos de aquí.

rows: One no before the verb. Do not repeat it before the noun.
A negative word after the verb needs no before the verb, and a person object takes personal a.
Personal a before a specific person.
In Spain the subject goes after the verb, or is left out.
y becomes e before i- and hi-.
o becomes u before o- and ho-.
Direction takes a, and a + el = al.
